description: Human rights groups report that 80% of women trafficked to Italy come from Benin City in Edo State, making it the main hub for sex trafficking between West Africa and Europe. UNICRI has cited Italy as the destination for more than 10,000 women trafficked from Benin City.
energy_note: Four fifths of them, from one city.

description: The IOM estimates 80% of Nigerian women travelling to Libya and then attempting the Mediterranean crossing are being trafficked into the European sex trade.
energy_note: Four in five of the women on those boats.

aspect: The debt, and the oath that enforces it
description: Before departure many women take part in a ceremony with a juju priest. Traffickers tell them they must obey or a curse will harm them. The oath-swearing commits the woman to repaying a debt, with violation supposedly leading to death or insanity. Repayment pacts have often been in the range of $40,000-$100,000.
energy_note: A hundred thousand dollars, secured on a curse.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the Oba's revocation, and what followed
description: In March 2018 the Oba of Benin, the most powerful traditional ruler in Benin City, issued a curse on traffickers and revoked all juju spells previously administered. The 2024 US Trafficking in Persons report notes traffickers continued performing juju ceremonies as a coercion tactic despite the revocation.
energy_note: The oath was cancelled by the man who could cancel it, and they kept using it.

description: In many cases parents and close relatives are implicated in the trafficking, which removes the obvious source of rescue and makes reporting an act against your own household.
energy_note: Reporting it means reporting your mother.

description: NAPTIP's Benin City office reported cases of intimidation and beatings against women refusing to pay debts, and threats against those asked to testify.
energy_note: The debt has collectors, at both ends.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the route shifts rather than closes
description: Research indicates the Libya returns increased awareness of the dangers and the difficulty of the crossing dissuaded Edo women from that route - but not from leaving Benin City, as they increasingly travel to other destinations. In one recent case 78 Nigerian girls trafficked to Côte d'Ivoire, some pregnant, were repatriated and received by NAPTIP at Lagos airport.
energy_note: Close one route and the destination changes, not the trade.

aspect: And the shelter at the end is not a solution
description: Human Rights Watch, in 'You Pray for Death', found many rescued victims kept in abhorrent conditions in Nigerian shelters similar to those they faced while trafficked, with authorities failing to provide resources to rebuild. As of March 2024 five organisations met NAPTIP's shelter standards.
energy_note: Rescued into conditions resembling the ones she was rescued from.
